reference.title: How We Feel, Story Burn Fire Animation (60fps.design): a card burns from the bottom edge to the top on one tap, a thin glowing rim on the burned edge, then the page's dark ground and a plain next screen; builds from REFERENCE.md (fields.burn, materials.paper scorch, lights.ember)

flash.tailSeconds.why: a measuring span, not a pass mark: the flash check steps a page from 0 to settle (6.15 s here) plus this tail. Bar 12 rests at its settle time: with the burn started (query burnAt=0), the frames at 6.15, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8.15, 9, 10 and 12 s are pixel-identical (largest difference 0 of 255, every step, seeds 1 to 3; measured 2026-11-19 with the page opened as the gate opens it). So the default 2 s tail repeats one frame and cannot hold a flash, and at about 0.25 s a frame in software WebGL it took the flash row to 123 s, over the 120 s every page test keeps. With 0 the check steps 0 to 6.15 s (370 frames) and still counts the whole burn, the front, the rim, the specks and the fade to the next screen.

beats: A paper card stands on a dark ground, its words printed on it; nothing moves until the user clicks the card or presses Enter on it
The burn starts in spots near the card's bottom edge and a torn front climbs to the top, racing and stalling, with holes and islands; the printed words burn away with the paper
Behind the front the paper darkens over a thin rim, about 5% of the card's width, from paper to char, and then it is gone: the page's dark ground shows through the hole
A thin hot rim runs along the hole's edge, a dim glow warms the paper ahead of the front and fades with distance, and glowing specks cool in the burned area until the last is out
When the card is gone the screen holds dark for a moment, then a plain next screen fades in; a second click does not start a second burn
